common_name: Cocktail Vodka Begonia (Bronze-Leaf Scarlet Wax Begonia)

planting.note: Start indoors 10–12 weeks before the last frost since Cocktail series begonias grow slowly from seed; transplant outdoors only after frost danger has fully passed. Vodka is a compact, bronze-leaved selection with scarlet-red flowers.

directions: Sow dust-fine seed on the surface of moist, sterile starting mix under bright light and do not cover, since the seed needs light to germinate and seedlings are slow to reach transplant size. Vodka carries glossy bronze-maroon foliage topped with masses of small scarlet-red flowers, and its dark leaf color lets it hold up in more direct sun than green-leaved wax begonias without scorching. It forms a tight, uniform mound that needs no deadheading and blooms non-stop from spring through the first hard freeze, making it a reliable edging plant for beds and containers in bright shade to morning sun.

common_name: Cocktail Whiskey Begonia (Bronze-Leaf White Wax Begonia)

planting.note: Start indoors 10–12 weeks before the last frost since Cocktail series begonias grow slowly from seed; transplant outdoors after frost danger has fully passed. Whiskey pairs dark bronze foliage with pure white flowers for high contrast in beds and pots.

directions: Sow dust-fine seed on the surface of moist, sterile starting mix under bright light without covering it, and expect slower growth than most bedding annuals before transplant size. Whiskey combines deep bronze-maroon leaves with pure white flowers, giving strong color contrast that reads well from a distance and brightens shaded corners where darker-flowered begonias can look muddy. Like other Cocktail series begonias its bronze foliage tolerates more direct sun than green-leaved wax begonias, and the compact, self-cleaning habit blooms continuously from spring until frost with no deadheading required.
